startup.name: Maywood
startup.one_liner: The first finance-compliant proactive AI that runs 24/7
startup.description: A proactive AI for dealmakers that runs in the background across network, pipeline and active processes, flags targets preparing for a process, drafts outreach, updates CRMs and builds meeting briefs, delivered by email, Teams or a platform. Five person team in New York. Buyers are banks and advisory firms.

yc_acceptance.basis: Note only because the company is already accepted. A random applicant starts near 1 percent. A five person team with a clear vertical, a compliance angle and a defined buyer would be above the base, held back by crowded AI assistants and unstated traction.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because the wedge sits between CRM and assistant products where Intapp DealCloud and Affinity already sell, and finance compliance procurement is slow. A reviewer would also ask why bankers would trust a new startup with sensitive deal data and whether a general AI product could do the same.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Failure paths are slow enterprise adoption, incumbent bundling and trust in sensitive deal data. If the product remains a nice feature, firms cancel after pilots, and the likely end is an acquisition by a CRM or data vendor for its customers and compliance setup. killers.risk: Incumbent deal CRM vendors add proactive AI
killers.evidence: Intapp markets DealCloud with an assistant and proactive relationship nudges for investment banks. and this pattern is visible in the cited analogs.
killers.mitigation: Integrate into DealCloud rather than replace it and win on the quality of proactive signals.

killers.risk: Bank compliance and security reviews stall adoption
killers.evidence: Finance buyers need data controls, audit trails and sign off, and a five person team may not have the certifications.
killers.mitigation: Get SOC 2 early and deploy inside the customer's environment.

killers.risk: General assistants from large AI labs cover the use case
killers.evidence: Email, meeting and research assistants are bundled into widely deployed productivity suites. and this pattern is visible in the cited analogs.
killers.mitigation: Rely on proprietary relationship graphs and deal data that a generic assistant cannot access.

killers.risk: Small buyer universe and long sales cycle
killers.evidence: Dealmaker teams are a limited set of firms, and pilots may not scale. and this pattern is visible in the cited analogs.
killers.mitigation: Expand to private equity and corporate development teams.

technical_complexity.rationale: Connecting email, Teams, news and CRM data and generating accurate briefs is standard AI engineering, but the compliance layer, permissioning and reliability for finance add real work. A five person team can build the core in three months but not enterprise grade controls.

takeover_risk.rationale: Incumbents already position AI for investment banking and own the CRM data and distribution. They could ship proactive features within a year, though a startup may move faster on quality.

evidence.claim: Intapp markets DealCloud as an AI platform for deal sourcing with proactive relationship nudges, which shows banks pay for this.

brand.rationale: A proper noun with a trustworthy sound but no meaning for the product. Invented or proper names are the most common kind in YC and show average survival, so it is neutral. Finance buyers care about security credentials more than the name.

narrative.headline: A sensible vertical AI wedge for dealmakers facing strong incumbents, likely to get a seed and a coin flip at Series A.
narrative.general_summary: Maywood sells a proactive assistant to dealmakers that tracks relationships and active processes. Banks already pay for deal CRMs, and the compliance angle is a real differentiator against general assistants. The risk is that Intapp, Affinity and Microsoft add similar features, and that adoption is slow. A seed above the YC check is likely for a five person vertical AI team in 2026. Reaching Series A depends on retention across deal teams and security approvals. About 40 percent of forecast paths end in a stall or shutdown.

assumptions: Blind forecast as of 2026-01-05 using only the batch listing.
Fintech cohorts are small (n=23 to 26), so B2B and AI cohorts were used as cross checks.
The step seed means a round above about $500K within roughly 12 months of the batch start.
